# 2 Kings Chapter 9 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 229v–231r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_009_page_001.jpg, 2KI_009_page_002.jpg, 2KI_009_page_003.jpg, 2KI_009_page_004.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** Then Elisha the prophet called one of the sons of the prophets and said to him, "Gird up your loins, take this flask of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth-gilead.

**2** When you arrive, look for Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi. Go in, get him away from his companions, and take him into an inner room.

**3** Then take the flask of oil and pour it on his head and say, 'Thus says the LORD: I anoint you king over Israel.' Then open the door and flee — do not delay."

**4** So the young man, the young prophet, went to Ramoth-gilead.

**5** When he arrived, the commanders of the army were sitting together. He said, "I have a message for you, commander." Jehu said, "For which of us?" He answered, "For you, commander."

**6** So Jehu arose and went into the house, and the young man poured the oil on his head and said to him, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: 'I anoint you king over the people of the LORD, over Israel.

**7** You shall strike down the house of Ahab your master, and I will avenge the blood of my servants the prophets and the blood of all the servants of the LORD, at the hand of Jezebel.

**8** The whole house of Ahab shall perish, and I will cut off from Ahab every male, bond and free, in Israel.

**9** I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah.

**10** And the dogs shall eat Jezebel in the plot of ground at Jezreel, and none shall bury her.'" Then he opened the door and fled.

**11** When Jehu came out to the servants of his master, one said to him, "Is all well? Why did this madman come to you?" He said to them, "You know the man and his talk."

**12** They said, "That is not true! Tell us." So he said, "Thus and so he spoke to me, saying, 'Thus says the LORD: I anoint you king over Israel.'"

**13** Then in haste each man took his garment and spread it under Jehu on the bare steps, and they blew the trumpet and proclaimed, "Jehu is king!"

**14** Thus Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi conspired against Joram. Now Joram with all Israel had been guarding Ramoth-gilead against Hazael king of Aram,

**15** but King Joram had returned to Jezreel to recover from the wounds that the Arameans had inflicted on him when he fought against Hazael king of Aram. Jehu said, "If this is your will, let no one escape from the city to go and tell the news in Jezreel."

**16** Then Jehu mounted his chariot and rode to Jezreel, for Joram was lying there. And Ahaziah king of Judah had come down to visit Joram.

**17** The watchman standing on the tower in Jezreel saw the company of Jehu as he approached and said, "I see a company." Joram said, "Send a horseman to meet them and ask, 'Do you come in peace?'"

**18** So the horseman went to meet him and said, "Thus says the king: 'Is it peace?'" Jehu said, "What have you to do with peace? Fall in behind me." The watchman reported, "The messenger reached them but has not returned."

**19** Then a second horseman was sent, who came to them and said, "Thus says the king: 'Is it peace?'" Jehu answered, "What have you to do with peace? Fall in behind me."

**20** The watchman reported, "He reached them but has not returned. And the driving is like the driving of Jehu son of Nimshi, for he drives furiously."

**21** Joram said, "Harness the chariot." When his chariot was harnessed, Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah set out, each in his own chariot, and went to meet Jehu. They met him at the plot of ground of Naboth the Jezreelite.

**22** When Joram saw Jehu, he said, "Is it peace, Jehu?" He answered, "What peace, so long as the harlotries and sorceries of your mother Jezebel are so many?"

**23** Then Joram turned about and fled, crying to Ahaziah, "Treachery, Ahaziah!"

**24** But Jehu drew his bow with all his strength and struck Joram between the shoulders. The arrow pierced his heart, and he sank down in his chariot.

**25** Jehu said to Bidkar his officer, "Pick him up and throw him on the plot of ground belonging to Naboth the Jezreelite. For remember — when you and I rode together behind Ahab his father, the LORD uttered this oracle against him:

**26** 'As surely as I saw yesterday the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons, declares the LORD, I will repay you on this plot of ground, declares the LORD.' Now then, pick him up and throw him on the plot of ground, in accordance with the word of the LORD."

**27** When Ahaziah king of Judah saw this, he fled in the direction of Beth-haggan. Jehu pursued him and said, "Shoot him also!" They struck him in his chariot at the ascent of Gur, near Ibleam, and he fled to Megiddo and died there.

**28** His servants carried him in a chariot to Jerusalem and buried him in his tomb with his fathers in the city of David.

**29** In the eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab, Ahaziah had begun to reign over Judah.

**30** When Jehu came to Jezreel, Jezebel heard of it. She painted her eyes, adorned her head, and looked down from the window.

**31** As Jehu entered the gate, she said, "Is it peace, you Zimri, murderer of your master?"

**32** He lifted his face to the window and said, "Who is on my side? Who?" Two or three eunuchs looked down at him.

**33** He said, "Throw her down." So they threw her down, and some of her blood spattered on the wall and on the horses, and he trampled her underfoot.

**34** Then he went in and ate and drank. He said, "See to this cursed woman and bury her, for she is a king's daughter."

**35** But when they went to bury her, they found nothing of her except the skull, the feet, and the palms of her hands.

**36** They came back and told him, and he said, "This is the word of the LORD, which he spoke by his servant Elijah the Tishbite: 'In the plot of ground at Jezreel the dogs shall eat the flesh of Jezebel,

**37** and the corpse of Jezebel shall be as dung on the face of the field in the plot of ground at Jezreel, so that no one can say: This is Jezebel's grave.'"

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Chapter 9 is the climax of a prophetic arc that stretches back to 1 Kings 19:16, where YHWH first commissioned the anointing of Jehu. The chapter is structured as a cascade: anointing (vv.1-13), pursuit (vv.14-21), execution of Joram (vv.22-26), execution of Ahaziah (vv.27-29), and the death of Jezebel (vv.30-37). The *shalom* refrain — asked five times, never answered positively — gives the chapter its thematic spine: there can be no peace while the house of Ahab stands. The death of Joram on Naboth's field completes the cycle of justice begun in 1 Kings 21. Jezebel's death scene is one of the Hebrew Bible's most cinematic passages — she prepares herself with royal dignity, delivers a devastating historical taunt, and meets her end with the same fierce power she wielded in life. The chapter raises hard questions: is Jehu an instrument of divine justice or a ruthless opportunist? The narrator presents both possibilities without resolution.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.8 — "every male" vs. literal Hebrew idiom
- **EMET:** "those who urinate against the wall [mashtin be-qir]"
- **LOGOS:** "every male"
- **PNEUMA:** "every last male"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "every male" — the Hebrew idiom *mashtin be-qir* is vulgar and formulaic. LOGOS's euphemistic rendering preserves the meaning while avoiding a phrase that distracts modern readers. EMET's literalism is noted in its brackets.

### V.11 — "madman" (meshugga')
- **All three:** "madman" (unanimous)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "madman" — all translators agree. The Hebrew *meshugga'* captures both the cultural dismissal of ecstatic prophets and the irony of the scene.

### V.22 — "harlotries and sorceries" vs. "prostitution and witchcraft"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "harlotries and sorceries"
- **PNEUMA:** "prostitution and witchcraft"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "harlotries and sorceries" — the Hebrew *zenunim* and *kheshafim* carry both literal and metaphorical weight (idolatry as spiritual adultery). The older English terms better preserve this dual register.

### V.24 — "between the shoulders" vs. "between the shoulder blades"
- **EMET:** "between his arms [zeroyotav]"
- **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** "between the shoulders/shoulder blades"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "between the shoulders" — the Hebrew *zeroyotav* can mean "arms" or the area between the shoulder blades. "Between the shoulders" is anatomically clearer for the narrative context (shot from behind while fleeing).

### V.30 — Jezebel's cosmetics: "paint" vs. "painted her eyes"
- **EMET:** "put paint [pukh] on her eyes"
- **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** "painted her eyes"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "painted her eyes" — *pukh* is kohl/antimony eye paint. "Painted her eyes" is clear and preserves the act of deliberate self-presentation. This is royal dignity, not seduction — all translators agree on this interpretation.

### V.31 — Rendering Jezebel's taunt
- **EMET:** "Is-[there] peace, Zimri, murderer of his master?"
- **LOGOS:** "Is it peace, you Zimri, murderer of your master?"
- **PNEUMA:** "Did you come in peace, Zimri — you who murdered your master?"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Is it peace, you Zimri, murderer of your master?" — LOGOS's rendering preserves the *shalom* refrain pattern while adding the contemptuous "you Zimri." PNEUMA's version loses the repetitive *ha-shalom* formula.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
